nodes.name: Thermal Annealing at 400°C
nodes.procedure: Bimetallic FeCoPBAs, monometallic CoPBA and FePBA underwent annealing at 400°C to introduce cyano vacancies (V_CN) while preserving structural integrity.

unit_operations.name: Thermal Annealing
unit_operations.procedure_snippet: bimetallic FeCoPBAs underwent annealing at temperatures of 300, 400, and 500°C... the PBA model precatalysts were annealed at 400°C to introduce defects

nodes.source_text: To introduce V_CN into MOFs while preserving their structural integrity, bimetallic FeCoPBAs underwent annealing at temperatures of 300, 400, and 500°C... Consequently, the PBA model precatalysts were annealed at 400°C to introduce defects for subsequent discussions, denoted as FeCoPBA-V_CN, FePBA-V_CN, and CoPBA-V_CN.

nodes.characterization_summary: Crystalline structure of bimetallic PBAs preserved at 400°C annealing with weaker diffraction pattern, destroyed at 500°C.
nodes.evidence_snippet: X-ray diffraction (XRD) was utilized to examine the effect of annealing on the crystalline structures of the bimetallic PBAs (Figure 1a). At 500°C, the crystalline structure of bimetallic PBAs is disrupted, yet it is still discernible albeit with a weaker diffraction pattern at 400°C.

nodes.characterization_summary: TGA validates thermal stability of as-prepared bimetallic PBAs with phase transition above 500°C.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Thermogravimetry analysis (TGA) validated the thermal stability of the as-prepared bimetallic PBAs.

nodes.characterization_summary: DSC shows two peaks: ≈120°C for absorbed water loss, second peak above 500°C for MOF phase transition.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Differential scanning calorimetry (DSC) showed two distinct peaks (Figure 1b): the first, ≈120°C, corresponds to the loss of absorbed water, while the second peak above 500°C corresponds to the phase transition of MOF structure.

nodes.characterization_summary: All samples show nanocubic crystals ≈150 nm with marginally increased surface roughness after 400°C annealing.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Scanning electron microscopy (SEM) and transmission electron microscopy (TEM) images (Figures S3 and S4, Supporting Information) revealed that all samples consisted of similar nanocubic crystals with an average size of ≈150 nm.

nodes.characterization_summary: ESR signal at g=2.02 ascribed to Co³⁺ unpaired electron, higher intensity indicates more CN vacancies; FeCoPBA-V_CN shows narrow-sharp peak.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The ESR signal (Figure 1c) at g = 2.02 was ascribed to the unpaired electron of Co³⁺, with higher ESR signal intensity indicating more concentrated CN vacancies.

nodes.characterization_summary: Co K-edge and Fe K-edge EXAFS fitting shows Co-N coordination number decreases from 5.8 to 5.2, Fe-C from 6.2 to 5.3; bond lengths Co-N 2.15→1.97 Å, Fe-C 1.96→1.87 Å indicating V_CN formation.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Moreover, the quantitative vacancy information of FeCoPBA-V_CN and FeCoPBA was compared by fitting the Co and Fe K-edge EXAFS data (Figure 1d,e; Tables S1 and S2, Supporting Information). After thermal annealing, the first coordination number of Co-N decreases from 5.8 to 5.2, and the Fe-C coordination number decreases from 6.2 to 5.3.

nodes.characterization_summary: FeCoPBA shows CN stretching at 2116 and 2158 cm⁻¹ (Fe²⁺-CN-Co³⁺, Fe³⁺-CN-Co²⁺); FeCoPBA-V_CN shows peaks at 2080, 2176, 2135 cm⁻¹ indicating Fe-CN-Fe and Co-CN-Co subunits.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The FT-IR spectra show significant shifts of peaks (Figure 2a), indicating the altered coordination structure of bimetallic PBAs.

nodes.characterization_summary: Co K-edge shifts to higher energy after annealing indicating oxidation >+3; Fe K-edge shifts to lower energy resembling Fe₂O₃ indicating predominant +3 state.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The K-edge of Co in CoPBA and FeCoPBA are both slightly shifted to higher energy after annealing (Figure 2b).

nodes.characterization_summary: Co 2p peaks of FeCoPBA-V_CN shift higher energy than CoPBA-V_CN indicating increased Co valence; Fe 2p fitting shows predominant Fe³⁺ in bimetallic vs reduction to Fe²⁺ in FePBA-V_CN.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Comparing CoPBA-V_CN and FeCoPBA V_CN, Co 2p peaks of FeCoPBA-V_CN slightly shift to higher energy, also suggesting the increased chemical valence of Co in bimetallic PBAs (Figure 2c).

nodes.characterization_summary: Double layer capacitance C_dl used to assess ECSA; FeCoPBA-V_CN shows 55.0 cm², FeCoPBA shows 65.9 cm².
nodes.evidence_snippet: To explore the electrocatalytic OER performance, double layer capacitance (C_dl) of the electrode was surveyed to assess the effective electrochemical active surface area (ECSA) (Figure 3a).

nodes.characterization_summary: FeCoPBA-V_CN shows lowest overpotential η=218 mV at 10 mA cm⁻²; highest TOF 0.167 s⁻¹ at 300 mV.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Linear sweep voltammetry (LSV) shows that FeCoPBA-V_CN exhibits the best OER activity with the lowest overpotential (η) of 218 mV at 10 mA cm⁻² among all PBAs (Figure 3b).

nodes.characterization_summary: FeCoPBA-V_CN shows smallest Tafel slope 39 mV dec⁻¹.
nodes.evidence_snippet: FeCoPBA-V_CN has the smallest Tafel slope of 39 mV dec⁻¹, outperforming FePBA-V_CN, CoPBA-V_CN, and FeCoPBA (82, 69, and 63 mV dec⁻¹, respectively) (Figure 3c).

nodes.characterization_summary: FeCoPBA-V_CN shows much lower charge transfer resistance R_ct than FeCoPBA.
nodes.evidence_snippet: FeCoPBA-V_CN presents much lower charge transfer resistance (R_ct) than FeCoPBA, confirming the faster kinetics of OER on FeCoPBA V_CN (Figure 3d).

nodes.characterization_summary: FeCoPBA-V_CN maintains constant potential over 30 h at 10 mA cm⁻².
nodes.evidence_snippet: The potential remains constant over 30 h, which proves the good stability of FeCoPBA-V_CN.

nodes.characterization_summary: FeCoPBA-V_CN fully activates in 30 CV cycles; FeCoPBA requires 800 CV cycles; Fe-CN/Co-CN peaks disappear.
nodes.evidence_snippet: While the complete activation of FeCoPBA-V_CN precursor was attained in 30 CV cycles (Figure 4a). In comparison, 800 CV cycles were required for the complete structural transformation to active FeCoPBA (Figure 4b).

properties.description: Graph showing intensity vs cycles, ESA activation, FeCPBA-Vc peaks at ~300, FeCPBA-Vcn at ~1000

nodes.characterization_summary: Prominent peak ≈680 cm⁻¹ confirms Fe,Co-OOH surface layer formation; better identified at 30 cycles for FeCoPBA-V_CN.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In situ Raman spectra on FeCoPBA-V_CN and FeCoPBA exhibit similar prominent peaks ≈680 cm⁻¹ which indicated the fabrication of Fe, Co-OOH surface layer after electrochemical activation.

nodes.characterization_summary: After 30 h OER, dissolved Fe from FeCoPBA-V_CN is 0.038 mg L⁻¹ vs 0.364 mg L⁻¹ from FeCoPBA; FePBA/FePBA-V_CN show 0.588-0.601 mg L⁻¹.
nodes.evidence_snippet: After 30 h OER, the dissolved Fe ion from FeCoPBA-V_CN is one-tenth of FeCoPBA (0.038 and 0.364 mg L⁻¹, respectively) detected by ICP-AES.

nodes.characterization_summary: EDX mapping shows FeCoPBA-V_CN maintains Fe/Co after 30 h; FePBA-V_CN loses most Fe.
nodes.evidence_snippet: EDX elemental mappings further reveal the process of Fe losing (Figure 4j-m).
